messages:

Cc: Marco Li <marco.li@stellardata.com>

Subject: Request: provisional uptime assurance & escrow for pilot ramp

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stellar's trial team is ready to start a six-week pilot next Monday, but our security/comms group flagged the SLA language around monthly credits. Given the ramp profile (heavy bursts during ET business hours) we want to request two things before we go live:

1) A provisional uptime assurance of 99.5% for the pilot term (instead of standard 99.9%) to account for burst-driven scheduling on your shared hosted tier.
2) Placement of potential monthly credits into a short-term escrow (documented and visible to our procurement) so we can reconcile any remedies quickly at pilot close.

I've attached a draft SLA with our suggested wording and a rollout plan. Can Redwood confirm whether these two concessions are possible for a time-limited pilot and what documentation you would need from our side?

Appreciate a compact response — we need to land legal sign-off by Thursday.

Best,
Sophie Trent
Head of Cloud Ops
Stellar Data Systems

Attachments: Stellar_SLA_Draft_20261011.pdf, Uptime_Rollout_Plan_Stellar_20261012.xlsx

Subject: Re: Request: provisional uptime assurance & escrow for pilot ramp

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Short answer: we can accommodate a temporary SLA adjustment for pilot customers, but there are a couple of guardrails we need to align on. High-level proposal from our side:

- Provisional uptime: Redwood can offer a time-boxed SLA of 99.5% for the pilot period (six weeks). We will mark this as an exception in the contract and include an automatic reversion to standard 99.9% at pilot close unless both parties agree to extend.

- Monthly credits escrow: We can record any eligible monthly service credits in an internal escrow/ledger for the duration of the pilot. At the end of the pilot we can either: (a) apply credits to Stellar's first invoice post-pilot, or (b) issue a one-time credit payment. We cannot transfer funds to a third-party escrow provider, but the ledger will be reflected in the invoice metadata and in your HubSpot deal record.

Questions before we finalise wording:
- Do you require a hard cap on credits during pilot months? (We typically propose a cap equal to the pilot monthly invoice.)
- Are there specific maintenance windows or blackout dates we should exclude?

Looping in Laura (contracts) and Ben (reliability) to confirm ops/legal implications.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — Vivek thanks for the summary. A few contract-level clarifications from our side:

1) Exception timeframe: Please state the exact pilot dates in the amendment (start/end). We'll include automatic reversion clause and an explicit change-control path if Stellar requests extension.

2) Credit calculation: Our standard remedy calculation (monthly credit as percentage of that month's invoice based on minutes of unavailability) will apply. For the pilot we can set a credit cap at 100% of the pilot monthly invoice for simple reconciliation. We will document credits in our billing system and annotate the invoice; that should meet procurement's visibility requirement.

3) Evidence requirements: To qualify for a remedy we need a logged incident with the usual RCA within 14 days. For pilot customers we can shorten that to 7 days to speed reconciliation.

Ben — any operational notes on maintenance carve-outs or planned capacity throttles?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Signature: Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: provisional uptime assurance & escrow for pilot ramp

Hi all —

Operational notes from reliability:

- Maintenance carve-outs: We'll keep the standard maintenance carve-out (scheduled maintenance notified 72 hours in advance). For the pilot we can offer a single maintenance blackout window during the core ramp week (to be scheduled with Stellar) that will not count against uptime calculations.
- Bursty traffic: Our routing can provision short-lived burst capacity but on hosted tiers we reserve the right to apply temporary throttling if system-wide thresholds are exceeded. Throttling events that are part of capacity enforcement won't qualify for credits.
- Observability: We'll provide a shared dashboard link during the pilot with token-level latency and availability metrics.

If Stellar accepts the 100% monthly-cap and shortened RCA window, I think we can proceed to sign the amendment this week.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

- Monthly credit cap set at 100% of the pilot month invoice.
- Shortened RCA window of 7 days for pilot incidents.
- One agreed maintenance blackout week during core ramp (Stellar to propose specific dates Monday).
